idiom_name: value assignment for value types + explicit Clone() (or a deep-copy helper) for graphs
implementation_notes: Go has no copy constructors and no clone interface; assignment copies self-contained values completely, but slice, map, pointer and channel fields keep sharing their backing data, so b := *a is a shallow copy in exactly the cases that matter. The idiomatic realization is therefore twofold: structs whose fields are values need no pattern at all (copy by assignment), while types that own mutable state expose an explicit Clone() method returning an independent value - or delegate to a deep-copy helper/generator (github.com/huandu/go-clone, doppel) for large graphs. An interface can declare Clone() Shape to get polymorphic cloning, but callers must then type-assert, and the method set must match the value/pointer receiver actually used.
pitfalls: b := *a copies the struct header but shares slices, maps and pointers; mutating through the copy is visible through the original (Go blog: 'the header gets copied but the array it points to is always shared').
The built-in copy(dst, src) copies only min(len(dst), len(src)) slice elements and does not follow pointers, so it is not a deep copy.
Method sets: Clone() on a value receiver copies the value each call, so it cannot reset per-instance state; Clone() on a pointer receiver means values (not pointers) do not satisfy the interface.
Reflection-based deep copy must special-case 'no-copy' types (sync.Mutex, atomic.Value) and handle cycles, or it corrupts state or loops.
